source: CARDI book "ដំណាំស្រូវនៅកម្ពុជា" (Rice Cultivation in Cambodia), by Men Sarom, Thuy Lina and Pheng Thimuny, published by CARDI, 2007. No elibrary URL visible; original tables cite Cambodia's Ministry of Agriculture Agricultural Statistics reports (1980-2000, 2001-2002, 2002-2003, 2003-2004, 2004-2005, 2005-2006) and Tichit, L. 1981, 'L'agriculture au Cambodge'.
text: This source traces the evolution of Cambodia's rice-growing area, yield, and total production across six historical periods: (1) Colonial protectorate period (1863-1953): rice area grew from roughly 0.5 million hectares (1863) to about 1.6 million hectares by 1953, with rice exported mainly through ports in French Cochinchina (southern Vietnam). (2) Independence and Sangkum Reastr Niyum period (1953-1970): area continued expanding, reaching roughly 2.5 million hectares, with average yield density in the range of about 1.0-1.3 tons/hectare. (3) Khmer Republic / civil war period (1970-1975): war severely disrupted production and rice exports, with large declines in cultivated area and yield as fighting spread through the countryside. (4) Democratic Kampuchea period (1975-1979): the Khmer Rouge imposed forced collectivization and large-scale irrigation/canal-digging labor campaigns; agricultural output collapsed and this period is associated with famine deaths - one commune-level figure cited (from Prum Tola and Bruce McKenney, 2002) recorded around 1,600 deaths from starvation. (5) People's Republic of Kampuchea / State of Cambodia period (1979-1989): rice farming was reorganized around solidarity groups (krom samaki); cultivated area recovered from roughly 1.4-1.9 million hectares in the early 1980s to about 2.6 million hectares by 1989, alongside gradually rising yields. (6) Contemporary period (1990-2005): Cambodia is reported to have reached rice self-sufficiency during 1990-1995; the modern research/extension system was built up through this period (see the companion CARDI/CIAP institutional-history entry); cultivated area reached about 2.7 million hectares by 2001; Cambodia recorded its first rice export surplus around 2002; flooding in 2003 reduced production in some provinces; and by 2004 national rice production is reported at roughly 4.7 million tons on an area of roughly 2.7-2.8 million hectares, despite continued localized flood and drought damage (for example, an estimated production loss on the order of 705,000 tons in flood/drought-affected provinces in 2004).
caveat: The source book also includes a detailed year-by-year statistical table (area, yield density, and total production) covering 1900-1989 and 2000-2005, drawn from Ministry of Agriculture Agricultural Statistics reports and Tichit (1981). That table uses Khmer-numeral formatting with periods as thousands separators, viewed via page rasterization (no reliable text layer - this source uses Limon-font encoding). Individual row-by-row figures could not be transcribed with confident precision (spot-checks of area x yield vs. reported production did not always reconcile cleanly, consistent with this project's experience that dense multi-column tables are the hardest OCR/vision-reading failure mode). The narrative period-level figures above come from the book's prose discussion, which was legible with much higher confidence, and are treated as the reliable content from this source. The detailed year-by-year table is noted here as existing in the source but not reproduced, rather than risking incorrect numbers; also note the table itself appears to skip 1990-1999 entirely (jumping from 1989 to 2000), which may reflect a genuine data gap from that unstable decade rather than a reading error on our part.
